prompt: Write exactly one concise image caption (one factual sentence, 10–30 words). Start with the subject: "[count + subject]" followed immediately by a present-participial action (e.g., "A woman whittling...", "Two players dribbling..."). Include 1–3 discriminative visual facts when clearly visible: counts, primary colors, specific objects/tools/clothing, and simple spatial relations ("next to", "behind", "left of"). Transcribe any readable letters or numbers exactly; if text is not legible, describe its appearance and placement (e.g., "white jersey with blue lettering on front"). Do not invent names, photographer credits, brands, dates, or background narratives. Prefer concrete action verbs over subjective adjectives; avoid emotion words unless clearly supported by pixels. Add one observable composition or lighting cue when applicable (viewpoint: "side/profile", "back-facing"; lighting: "sunlit", "long shadows"). Output only the single caption sentence—no lists, tags, JSON, extra metadata, or multiple candidates. Template to follow: "[Count + subject] [present-participial verb] [object/location], wearing [distinct clothing], [holding/using object]; [short scene or lighting/viewpoint cue]."
